hero.lead: Resomix helps people discover sonically related tracks, understand one recording in greater detail and make authorised catalogues searchable through sound.
hero.support: One proprietary engine, PYXIS-1, powers three distinct products built around the recording itself.
hero.status: Live production beta · Sonic Discovery · Track Intelligence · Catalogue Intelligence
hero.captionB: A COMPANY PROPOSITION · NOT A USER WORKFLOW

hero.title: A sonic intelligence platform for those who [[feel the music.]]

mission.h2: Build tools that listen to the recording itself.
mission.body1: The ability to tell a story through sound is a deeply human trait. Woven into the history of our species, music connects people and intensifies emotion in ways few other art forms can.
mission.body2: With Resomix, we are building a platform that works beyond tags, popularity signals and static metadata. It starts from the audio recording and uses measurable sonic characteristics to support discovery and understanding.
mission.body3: By analysing structure, harmony, rhythm, timbre, spectral character and energy, Resomix opens three distinct routes: find sonically related tracks, examine one recording in greater detail, or make an authorised catalogue searchable by sound.
mission.interp: Metadata tells us what a recording is called. Audio analysis gives us another way to understand how it moves, feels and relates to other recordings.
mission.figureAria: A metadata frame containing title, artist, genre, release date and label surrounds the audio-derived evidence: five characteristic bands and seventy-plus measurable characteristics.

evidence.h2: Music discovery should go deeper than tags and trends.
evidence.body1: Resomix began with a frustration familiar to DJs, curators and music professionals: spending hours moving through stores, platforms and catalogues to find the recording that fits a particular moment.
evidence.body2: PYXIS-1, our proprietary audio-analysis and similarity engine, preprocesses recordings and extracts more than 70 measurable characteristics across rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure, spectral profile and energy.
evidence.body3: It creates a sonic profile that can be read through Track Intelligence or compared with recordings already processed into an applicable index. Similarity results are ranked automatically according to the closest measured sonic relationships.
evidence.status: Proprietary algorithm · Audio-derived evidence · Human decision
evidence.figureAriaD: One recording enters; five characteristic bands and seventy-plus characteristics form one sonic profile; the profile supports two possible operations: read one recording through Track Intelligence, or compare with an index for ranked similarity.
evidence.figureAriaM: Mobile: one recording, five bands, one sonic profile, two possible operations.
evidence.interp: PYXIS-1 turns measurable audio characteristics into a sonic profile that can be examined or compared.

evolution.h2: One human problem. Three distinct ways to work with sound.
evolution.intro: The first question was simple: if one track feels right, what should come next? Building that discovery engine revealed two further needs: understanding the recording in greater detail and bringing the same sound-first search into authorised catalogues.

sd.title: Sonic Discovery
sd.body: Start with one known track or upload a reference. PYXIS-1 compares its sonic profile with a pre-analysed index and returns the closest matches as an automatically ranked Sonic Discovery playlist.
sd.figureAria: One orange reference passes the comparison ring and returns a compact ranked list, with the strongest orange on result one.

ti.qLabel: What is happening inside this recording?
ti.title: Track Intelligence
ti.body: Examine one recording through a readable view of its structure, rhythm, harmony, energy, timbre, spectral character and the confidence behind key outputs.
ti.figureAria: A time axis with structural regions and a readable energy journey, with one selected moment and its interpretation.

ci.qLabel: How can this catalogue be searched by sound?
ci.title: Catalogue Intelligence
ci.body: Process authorised catalogue recordings into a private, partner-scoped sonic index. Use one reference to retrieve the closest recordings from that catalogue, with Track Intelligence available separately when deeper examination is needed.
ci.outcome: Authorised catalogue → private index → ranked partner results
ci.figureAria: A heavy partner boundary holds pre-processed recording cells; one approved reference query returns a ranked result list. No shared catalogue pool.

api.label: For platforms & music technology
api.body: Partners can bring similarity and track-analysis capabilities into their own products through a scoped API and guided integration while keeping their interface, brand and customer journey.

vision.h2: Make sound itself a route into discovery.
vision.body1: We want to make analysing and discovering music faster and more useful. We imagine a world where a recording’s visibility is not determined only by chart position, marketing budget, recency or the accuracy of its tags.
vision.body2: Resomix builds a sonic profile from measurable characteristics and uses it to reveal relationships that metadata alone may not show. The aim is not to replace listening, taste or professional judgement. It is to help them travel further.
vision.statement: The recording deserves another way to be found.
vision.figureAriaD: A low-exposure recording sits mostly outside the visible field with a restrained orange rim; its measured relationship to a known reference surfaces it as ranked candidate number three.
vision.figureAriaM: Mobile: the low-exposure recording, its relationship to a known reference, and its return as ranked candidate three.
vision.interp: Relevance should not disappear with release date. A recording can return to view when its measured sonic relationship to a reference is strong.

principles.h2: Measurable sound. Clear outputs. Human judgement.
principles.intro: Resomix combines proprietary processing and ranking with established audio-analysis tools to create a practical sonic profile for each recording.

p1.title: Audio-derived evidence
p1.body: PYXIS-1 works from the recording, extracting more than 70 measurable characteristics across verified sonic dimensions.

p2.title: Read or compare
p2.body: A sonic profile can support a readable Track Intelligence view or be compared with an applicable pre-analysed index. These are distinct workflows.

p3.title: Results in seconds
p3.body: Existing indexed references return faster. Uploaded references take longer because they must first be processed. Similarity results are ranked automatically.

p4.title: Human decision
p4.body: Resomix surfaces evidence and candidates. DJs, producers, curators and catalogue teams make the final call.

chainNote.body: Every returned result can become a new starting point after the playlist has been delivered, allowing a listener to follow a new sonic direction without changing how the original ranking was created.
chainNote.figureAria: A chain of three reference cells, each becoming the next starting point after a playlist is returned.

shelf.h2: Relevance should not expire with release date.
shelf.body1: Every catalogue has a quieter layer of tracks that did not reach the charts, albums that fell through algorithmic cracks and artists whose work sits outside the spotlight.
shelf.body2: Resomix can bring a recording back into view when it is sonically relevant to a reference. It does not predict commercial success or guarantee exposure. It creates another evidence-based route into discovery.
shelf.figureAriaD: Rows of catalogue recordings arranged by release order; one older recording receives a sonic relationship from the active reference and moves into the ranked output row, its release date visible.
shelf.figureAriaM: Mobile: the older catalogue recording is matched through sonic relevance and appears in the ranked output with its release date visible.

values.h2: Technology should expand human listening, not pretend to replace it.

v1.title: The art of personal curation
v1.body: You still make the call. Resomix helps you get there faster by surfacing candidates and evidence that support deeper listening.

v2.title: Another route for less-visible music
v2.body: Sound-first retrieval can give older and lower-exposure recordings another chance to surface when they are relevant to a reference.

v3.title: Clear boundaries
v3.body: Temporary user references and partner catalogue assets follow separate handling paths. Each partner catalogue and sonic index remains inside its authorised scope.

v4.title: Precision over volume
v4.body: Resomix returns ranked results and lets the user choose the available result depth. More results are not automatically better results.

audiences.h2: Built for people who make decisions through sound.

items.title: DJs
items.body: Reduce crate digging and find tracks that fit the energy, groove and character of a set.

items.title: Producers
items.body: Inspect arrangement, energy, timbre and sonic character in a recording, then explore related references while keeping the creative decision yours.

items.title: Music curators
items.body: Start from an audio reference and review a ranked set of sonically related candidates beyond charts and static metadata.

items.title: Music enthusiasts
items.body: Explore new sonic relationships from one known recording and follow the directions that feel meaningful.

items.title: Record labels and distributors
items.body: Make authorised catalogue recordings searchable by sound and retrieve ranked catalogue matches from one reference.

items.title: Music publishers
items.body: Explore represented recordings through sound and support human catalogue and licensing research without replacing rights judgement.

items.title: Sync agencies
items.body: Use an audio reference to surface candidates for human review. Resomix does not automate clearance, rights decisions or placement.

items.title: Music libraries and sample providers
items.body: Help authorised audio libraries be explored through structure, texture and sonic relationships.

items.title: Platforms and music technology
items.body: Integrate partner-scoped similarity and track-analysis capabilities through a guided API integration.

partners.h2: Make an authorised catalogue searchable through sonic relationships.
partners.body1: Partners provide agreed audio and metadata for processing. Resomix creates a private, partner-scoped sonic index that can return ranked catalogue results or support separate track-level intelligence through a guided pilot and scoped integration.
partners.body2: Partners retain their rights, branding, storefront, transaction flow and customer relationship. Resomix does not generate derivative audio, does not use partner content to train or fine-tune its systems, and does not place one partner’s catalogue inside another partner’s index.
partners.body3: The public beta and every partner evaluation must use audio that Resomix is authorised to process.
partners.figureAriaD: Authorised audio and agreed metadata are processed by PYXIS-1 into a private sonic index inside one partner scope, returning ranked partner output, with Track Intelligence as a separate option.
partners.figureAriaM: Mobile: the partner flow from authorised audio through PYXIS-1 into the private index, ranked output and the separate Track Intelligence option.

team.h2: Built by people who have spent years searching for the right track.
team.body1: Resomix was born from a frustration familiar to many music professionals: spending hours exploring platforms and catalogues to find the music needed for a project or DJ set.
team.body2: We are a small team of music-industry professionals and signal-processing engineers based in Thessaloniki, Greece, building the discovery and intelligence tools we wished existed.
team.figureAria: A studio workbench composition: Thessaloniki coordinates, a small hardware console grid, and a timeline from music practice through signal processing to product building.

founder.quote1: “I discovered electronic music through Italian progressive house radio in the late 1990s. Two decades of DJing and producing taught me one thing: finding the right track is the hardest part of the creative process.
founder.quote2: Resomix is the tool I needed and could not find: built on signal processing, not hype. After creating our discovery engine, I realised people across the music sector could benefit from the same foundation, not only DJs but also producers, supervisors, publishers and catalogue owners. Resomix is designed to show connections and enhance human curation across the industry.”
founder.figureAriaD: A restrained analogue radio-frequency line beginning at Italian progressive house radio in the late 1990s, carrying twenty-plus years of DJing and producing, and resolving into the present Resomix signal in Thessaloniki.
founder.figureAriaM: Mobile: the late-1990s radio-frequency line resolving into the present Resomix signal.
